name: sqlpp23
listed_description: A type safe SQL library for C++. (BSD-2-Clause)
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README and docs have no performance statements (docs/differences_to_sqlpp11.md and docs/README.md mention only compile-time type checking), the repo root has no benchmark directory (cmake, docs, examples, include/sqlpp23, modules, scripts, tests), and a WebSearch for sqlpp11/sqlpp23 benchmarks vs raw SQLite, SQLiteCpp or SOCI found nothing. It is a query-builder library with no speed claim at all.

name: TigerBeetleDB C++ client
listed_description: TigerBeetle is a financial accounting database designed for mission critical safety and performance to power the future of financial services. (BSL-1.0)
reason: No baseline comparison. The repo is a header-only C++20 wrapper over TigerBeetle's C client (13 stars); its only number is sample program output ('194 transfers per second', 819,100 transfers) with no other client or database to compare against, and the root has no benchmark directory. TigerBeetle's own performance claims belong to the upstream Zig database, not this wrapper.

name: Trilogy
listed_description: a client library for MySQL-compatible database servers, designed for performance, flexibility, and ease of embedding. (MIT)
reason: Directional claim only. The README says 'designed for performance' with no numbers. contrib/ruby/script/benchmark is a benchmark-ips script that compares trilogy with mysql2 (connect, escape, ping, query, large query) but the repo publishes no results; issue #7 (Benchmarks and experience from prod?) has no numbers, only the author's recollection that execution and allocation performance were 'slightly better' than mysql2; PR #212 (Speed up Trilogy#escape, 239.7k to 1.039M i/s) compares old vs new Trilogy, not another client; issue #224 reports a slowdown vs mysql2. A third-party dev.to benchmark post exists but dev.to is blocked here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so no mysql2 numbers could be opened.
